title: OpenAI-compat: Support Responses API variants + seed/determinism flags and metadata passthrough
author: Maya Singh
description:
Problem: The OpenAI Responses API introduced a set of semantics (responses vs completions, explicit seed/determinism controls, and response-level metadata passthrough) that our OpenAI-compatibility layer did not fully honor. This caused incorrect caching behavior, sporadic nondeterministic results in determinism test suites, and loss of user-supplied metadata when proxying requests.

This PR implements end-to-end support for the new Responses API variants in the compatibility shim, including: mapping `responses.mode` to appropriate model routing, plumbing `seed` and `deterministic` flags through to our runtime so user-requested determinism is honored, and preserving arbitrary `metadata` objects from request -> internal request -> response. It also includes several small streaming stability fixes uncovered while testing long-running streaming responses (fragment reassembly and backpressure on partial tool calls).

What changed (high level):
- Add a Responses-compatible request parser that accepts both completions and responses shapes and normalizes to our internal request model.
- Expose `seed` and `deterministic` parameters in the OpenAI-compat layer and ensure those are communicated to the runtime scheduling/kernel selection codepath so quantization/batching heuristics avoid interfering with deterministic runs.
- Preserve `metadata` keys on the proxied request and include them verbatim on the returned response envelope; add whitelist-based passthrough config for enterprise users wanting stronger controls.
- Streaming fixes: ensure partial tool/function call events include metadata and stream markers in the same envelope to avoid reassembly ambiguity for clients. Add idempotent reassembly on the client-side helper we publish in the SDKs.
- Tests: add unit and integration tests for parse/serialize roundtrips, deterministic seeds, and an end-to-end streaming canary that exercises large payload streaming + metadata passthrough.

Checklist:
- [x] Compatibility parsing and normalization
- [x] Runtime flags plumbing (seed/deterministic)
- [x] Metadata passthrough + enterprise whitelist config
- [x] Streaming reassembly fixes and unit tests
- [x] Integration canary and e2e tests in eval-harness
- [x] Documentation snippets and migration notes in redwood-docs

Design notes and rationale:
- Determinism is best-effort across lower-level optimizations. We mark requests with determinism metadata and ensure the scheduler selects single-worker, non-batched execution when deterministic=true or seed is set. This increases latency/cost for those requests; documentation and telemetry flag these requests separately so customers can understand tradeoffs.
- Metadata passthrough is implemented as a minimal-copy envelope change at the compatibility shim boundary; we deliberately avoid schema enforcement in the shim and provide an enterprise toggle to enforce a server-side whitelist for regulated customers.
- Streaming: inconsistent partial envelopes were the main cause of reassembly bugs — we now include sequence numbers and a final=true marker for tool call closures; SDK helpers were adjusted accordingly.

Backward compatibility and migration: The shim accepts both old completions-style requests and the newer responses payloads. Most customers require no change. For deterministic workloads, customers should set `deterministic: true` or provide `seed` to get reproducible outputs; documentation link: https://docs.redwood.ai/openai-compat#responses-determinism

Rollout plan:
- Feature behind compat flag `openai_responses_v2` on the tenancy and account level.
- Canary rollout to 2% of traffic for 48 hours with synthetic prompts exercising streaming and deterministic paths.
- Monitor token-latency, deterministic-error-rate, and metadata-loss metrics in console.

Related: Linear ENG-4821, PM-219. See also the eval-harness PR that adds the deterministic test vectors.
